stem: What does nutrient antagonism mean in plant nutrition?
choices: A high level or imbalance of one ion can interfere with the uptake or use of another nutrient
A rise in total solution EC makes each nutrient less available in roughly the same proportion because ions compete equally for root uptake
Plants shift nutrient uptake toward whichever elements are most concentrated in the root zone, reducing the importance of nutrient ratios
Micronutrients offset excess macronutrients by binding them in the root zone, so increasing trace elements can correct most ion imbalances
rationale: Nutrients interact. Excess or imbalance of one ion can reduce uptake or physiological use of another, which is why diagnosis should consider ratios and root-zone conditions rather than simply adding more fertilizer.
